style: mid-90s New York hip-hop, a 9pm FM countdown promo built into a rap song, 90 BPM, sparse and grimy. A DJ scratches a loud booming announcer voice shouting each number, one cut per number, landing on beat one, stuttered and chopped. Heavy thumping kick, cracking dry snare on two and four, faint shaker, a single ominous low piano chord struck once a bar and left to ring, round sub bass, wide silences between hits. Solo male rapper, heavyset Brooklyn voice: deep, thick, raspy, nasal edge, lazy confident drawl, calm menace with a grin, talks the rules like a big brother laying it out at the table, every syllable clear, words dragged late against the snare, vocal tight and in your ear, dry
exclude: trap, 808 rolls, autotune, sung hook, melodic rap, female vocals, choir, strings, reverb, EDM, lo-fi chill, saxophone, high-pitched voice, double-time, pop polish, live band
lyrics:
[Intro: dry ad-lib, close to the mic, needle hiss]
Uh. Money printer manual. Take notes.

[Scratch cut: announcer voice shouts "one"]
[Rap: deep, lazy, menacing grin]
Number one: never tell 'em what you printed,
trillions out the back door, keep the ledger tinted.

[Scratch cut: announcer voice shouts "two"]
Number two: never get high on your own supply,
banks took the first hit, now the rent's sky-high.

[Scratch cut: announcer voice shouts "three"]
Number three: no consignment, cash up front, that's law,
they took the bailout on tick and they ain't paid at all.

[Drums cut, piano chord rings alone, spoken low]
And the fix, from the future? No hand on the printer.

[Outro: one final scratch, hard stop]
title: tec-r2-radio-promo-countdown
